name: The daughters of Zelophehad
charge: Asking rightly for their father's inheritance, and marrying within their tribe as commanded
summary: Five sisters with no brother came to the door of the tabernacle and asked why their father's name should be done away from among his family because he had no son. The Lord said, The daughters of Zelophehad speak right, and made a statute of judgment for all Israel. They then married as they were told, and kept the inheritance in Manasseh.
offense: Five women with no brother came to the door of the tabernacle and made a legal argument, and the record names them, Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah, and names their tribe, Manasseh (Numbers 27:1). They did not ask for pity and they did not accuse anyone. They set out the facts: our father died in the wilderness, and he was not in the company of them that gathered themselves together against the Lord in the company of Korah, but died in his own sin, and had no sons (Numbers 27:3). Then the question, and it was the question of the lineage: why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son? give unto us therefore a possession among the brethren of our father (Numbers 27:4). They brought a gap in the law to the only authority who could fill it, in the proper form and at the proper place, and Moses did not answer out of his own judgment: Moses brought their cause before the Lord (Numbers 27:5). When the answer created a second question, that an inheritance might pass out of the tribe by marriage, the chief fathers of Gilead brought that too (Numbers 36:1-4), and the daughters accepted the further ruling and married within their father's tribe as commanded (Numbers 36:10-12).
judgment: The Lord did not merely grant the request; he endorsed the reasoning: the daughters of Zelophehad speak right, thou shalt surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father's brethren (Numbers 27:7). Their case became the order of inheritance for the whole nation: if a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter, and if he have no daughter, to his brethren, and if no brethren, to his father's brethren, and if his father have no brethren, to his kinsman that is next to him of his family, and it shall be unto the children of Israel a statute of judgment (Numbers 27:8-11). entries.commentary: The daughters of Zelophehad, of the tribe of Manasseh, stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the princes, and all the congregation at the door of the tabernacle. Their father died in the wilderness in his own sin; he was not in the company of Korah that gathered together against the Lord. He had no sons, only these five daughters. Their question was the question of the lineage: since the man puts the seed in the woman, if a man had only daughters, why should his name be done away from among his family? So they asked for a possession among the brethren of their father.

Moses brought their cause before the Lord. He did not do his own thing; he sought counsel and asked the Most High what to do in this instance. The Lord said the daughters of Zelophehad speak right: give them a possession of an inheritance among their father's brethren, and cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them.

Here the Lord set the order of inheritance for all Israel: if a man die and have no son, it passes to his daughter; if no daughter, to his brethren; if no brethren, to his father's brethren; and if his father had no brethren, to the kinsman that is next to him of his family. Every angle was covered so the inheritance stayed within the tribe. Israel always had questions, just as we do when we read, and the Lord put these statutes in place to answer them before they were asked. But what if a daughter who received the inheritance married into another tribe? You have to go precept upon precept: [Numbers 36](/bible/numbers/36) takes up that very case with these same daughters. The chief fathers of Gilead brought it to Moses, and the word came back that the daughters of Zelophehad may marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.

The Lord told Moses to get up into mount Abarim and see the land given to the children of Israel; he would see it but not enter it, and then be gathered unto his people as Aaron his brother was gathered. The reason is written: Moses rebelled against the commandment of the Most High in the desert of Zin at the water of Meribah. The Lord gave a specific commandment to speak unto the rock before their eyes, and Moses instead smote the rock twice; the water still came out abundantly, but Moses and Aaron did not sanctify the Lord in the eyes of the children of Israel, and for that neither of them brought the congregation into the land.

Before his death Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation, to go out before them and come in before them, to lead them out and bring them in, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd. Moses asked for a man because the leadership of the nation belongs to men. The woman was made to be an help meet unto the man, not to rule over him; she is the weaker vessel, and the congregation is not set up for her to lead it. A sister helping to build up other sisters new in the congregation is right, and the sisters bless the nation with real talents, raising the children in the commandments, and the aged women teaching the young women. But teaching and leading the nation is not the place the Most High set for her.

The Lord answered: take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him. Joshua was set before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation and given his charge in their sight, and some of Moses' honour was put upon him, so all Israel could see with their own eyes the man the Most High ordained to lead the nation after the death of Moses. Joshua was to stand before Eleazar the priest, who would ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord; at his word they would go out and come in, he and all the children of Israel with him.

Moses did as the Lord commanded him: he took Joshua, set him before Eleazar the priest and all the congregation, laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses.

The chief fathers of the families of Gilead of the tribe of Manasseh bring an issue rising out of what was already ruled in Numbers 27: when Zelophehad died in the wilderness with no sons, the Lord ruled that his inheritance pass to his daughters. Their concern is real: if the daughters marry men of another tribe, their father's inheritance passes with them to the husband's tribe, and at the jubilee it is fixed to that tribe, so the tribe of Manasseh loses that land forever.

The Most High affirms the tribe of the sons of Joseph: they have said well. The solution: the daughters of Zelophehad may marry whom they think best, only within the family of the tribe of their father. The purpose is stated plainly: so shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe; the marriage boundary here was instituted because of land inheritance.

Every daughter that possessed an inheritance had to marry within her father's tribe, so every man of Israel would enjoy the inheritance of his fathers and no inheritance would remove from one tribe to another. The tribal restriction belonged to the time when Israel dwelt in the land; it existed because of inheritance. Today Israel has no inheritance in the lands of captivity, so the rule that still applies is marrying within the nation of Israel, not tribe-only marriage. No one today knows his exact tribe with certainty; a Judahite could have been dropped off anywhere in the captivity. Without the history of [Numbers 36](/bible/numbers/36), [Tobit 4:12](/bible/tobit/4#v12) gets twisted into a doctrine that a man may only marry his own tribe, and that is a heresy born of not knowing why the law was given.

The daughters of Zelophehad did as the Lord commanded Moses: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah married their father's brothers' sons, within the families of Manasseh, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father. These are the commandments and the judgments which the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho; with this verse the book of Numbers is completed. --- Topics: [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

A lot goes into an allotment, a portion; there was a portion for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was the firstborn of Joseph. Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh and the father of Gilead, was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan. Bashan was the kingdom of Og, one of the giants that Israel conquered under Joshua. Before the conquest all this territory was called the land of Canaan, with the Canaanites, the Perizzites, and the Jebusites and their families dwelling in it. Prior to this chapter Judah received his inheritance in chapter 15 and the inheritance of Joseph, Ephraim, came in chapter 16; after the victories the Most High gave through Christ, the land was divided by lot so that every tribe had its portion. The Bible maps that even the enemies of Israel put together according to the scriptures show this history: Manasseh held Bashan and a portion by Gilead on the other side of Jordan. The so-called Cubans come from this tribe; this is their history that their enemies do not want them to know.

There was also a lot for the rest of the children of Manasseh by their families, Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida: these were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph. Remember that Manasseh was the son of Joseph; Joseph had two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh.

Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. They came near before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying the Lord commanded Moses to give them an inheritance among their brethren; and according to the commandment of the Lord he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father.

Ten portions fell to Manasseh, beside the land of Gilead and Bashan which were on the other side of Jordan. On the map the Jordan river flows down through the land, and across the river sat Gilead and Bashan, the lands Manasseh already held. Down south the Jordan empties into the Dead Sea, and Sodom and Gomorrah sat south of the Dead Sea, by where Edom was residing; the maps give a good feel for what the Bible is talking about. The daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons, just as the Lord commanded for the daughters of Zelophehad, and the rest of Manasseh's sons had the land of Gilead.

The coast of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethah; Manasseh had the land of Tappuah, but Tappuah itself on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim. We have to know where our forefathers came from and what the Bible is speaking about; that is why we search out these borders on the maps, where Tappuah sat on the southern border by Shechem.

The coast descended to the river Kanah: southward of the river the cities were Ephraim's, and northward it was Manasseh's, the sea was his border, and they met together in Asher on the north and in Issachar on the east. This land of Canaan is also known as Israel, and this is where our foremothers and forefathers lived: the so-called Mexicans, Guatemalans, and Hondurans lived here, and the so-called Brazilians, Colombians, and Venezuelans up in these coasts. A lot of times we read that Asher lived here and forget it is talking about us; our people need the visual. Manasseh also had within Issachar and Asher the cities of Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor, En-dor, Taanach, and Megiddo with their towns, even three countries.

Even though Israel conquered the majority of the land of Canaan, there were still areas the Canaanites kept possession of; the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities, but the Canaanites would dwell in that land. When the children of Israel were waxen strong, they put the Canaanites to tribute, but did not utterly drive them out; they kept them as servants and handmaids.

The children of Joseph, led by Ephraim, asked Joshua why he gave them but one lot to inherit, seeing they are a great people; great here means numerous. Ephraim and Manasseh were among the most populated tribes, and Ephraim's own portion had already been given back in chapter 16. Their fruitfulness was prophesied when Israel blessed Joseph; the very name Ephraim goes into being fruitful.

The children of Joseph answered that the hill is not enough for them, and the Canaanites that dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron; those nations had military power too. On the map those Canaanites sat right north of Manasseh, in Beth-shean and her towns and in the valley of Jezreel, dwelling in the midst of our brothers with an army; they were a problem, and Manasseh was already having a hard time with them.

Joshua told the house of Joseph, thou art a great people and hast great power; the mountain shall be thine, and thou shalt drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots and though they be strong. Going through the wood means going through the dense forest; it would be a struggle, but at the end of the day they would overcome. Manasseh had issues driving the Canaanites out, but Ephraim did it. The difference between the two brothers goes back to [Genesis 48](/bible/genesis/48), where Israel blessed Joseph's sons and crossed his hands, guiding them wittingly, meaning he knew exactly what he was doing.

The sons of Issachar are named, and the heads of their fathers' houses are counted as valiant men of might in their generations. In the days of David their number was two and twenty thousand and six hundred, and reckoned by all their genealogies they were fourscore and seven thousand mighty men.

The sons of Benjamin are set down, Bela, Becher, and Jediael, with the heads of their houses reckoned as mighty men of valor. Issachar and Benjamin were warriors, not a joke. Our brethren have always been warriors who only lost their spirit in these last days.
The sons of Naphtali are named, and the sons of Manasseh through his concubine, down to the line of Gilead. The daughters of Zelophehad are noted, and the sons of Gilead are set in order.

The sons of Ephraim are traced, and Ezer and Elead are named, whom the men of Gath slew when they came down to take their cattle. Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him, and afterward Beriah was born and the line continued to Joshua, with their possessions and habitations named.

The sons of Asher are named, and their line is traced through the heads of their fathers' houses. Asher were warriors too, choice and mighty men of valor, chief of the princes, numbered twenty and six thousand men fit for the battle.

verses.text: Then came the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of Manasseh the son of Joseph: and these are the names of his daughters; Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.
And they stood before Moses, and before Eleazar the priest, and before the princes and all the congregation, by the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, saying,
Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not in the company of them that gathered themselves together against the Lord in the company of Korah; but died in his own sin, and had no sons.
Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son? Give unto us therefore a possession among the brethren of our father.
And Moses brought their cause before the Lord.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

The daughters of Zelophehad speak right: thou shalt surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father’s brethren; and thou shalt cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them.
And thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter.
And if he have no daughter, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his brethren.
And if he have no brethren, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his father’s brethren.

And if his father have no brethren, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his kinsman that is next to him of his family, and he shall possess it: and it shall be unto the children of Israel a statute of judgment, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And Moses commanded the children of Israel according to the word of the Lord, saying, The tribe of the sons of Joseph hath said well.
This is the thing which the Lord doth command concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, Let them marry to whom they think best; only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.
So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe: for every one of the children of Israel shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.

And every daughter, that possesseth an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Israel, shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that the children of Israel may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.
Neither shall the inheritance remove from one tribe to another tribe; but every one of the tribes of the children of Israel shall keep himself to his own inheritance.
Even as the Lord commanded Moses, so did the daughters of Zelophehad:
For Mahlah, Tirzah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, were married unto their father’s brothers’ sons:
And they were married into the families of the sons of Manasseh the son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father.

But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters: and these are the names of his daughters, Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

And they came near before Eleazar the priest, and before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying, The Lord commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brethren. Therefore according to the commandment of the Lord he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father.
And there fell ten portions to Manasseh, beside the land of Gilead and Bashan, which were on the other side Jordan;
Because the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons: and the rest of Manasseh’s sons had the land of Gilead.
And Machir took to wife the sister of Huppim and Shuppim, whose sister’s name was Maachah;) and the name of the second was Zelophehad: and Zelophehad had daughters.
